items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Well, I won't hear when she died. Yeah. Maybe she was. But I was in Chicago.

ctx.x: I think Miss Cole was buried with music.
Well, I won't hear when she died. Yeah. Maybe she was. But I was in Chicago. Uh-huh.
Well, are young guys ever buried with music? I mean... Or do you have to be a certain age to be buried with music?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: But what about Miss Cole's lawn parties?

ctx.x: I was just at Fing and Willows. Yeah, I played there a couple of times too. A little yard, you know? Yeah. I mean we played there every Monday night, Sunday night.
But what about Miss Cole's lawn parties?

That was just at Fing and Willows. Yeah, I played there a couple of times too. And used to have a little place right back of Perdita Street there. A little yard, you know? Yeah. Right there. Perdita and Satova, I think. It was a Franklin. One of them streets. But that's where Lewis used to get off the boat and come catch me playing there all the time to sit in and play with me.
